subject: Post-call: Unit-econ & pricing next steps / pilot proposal
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finserve.com>
Cc: Jae Kim <jae.kim@finserve.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call: Unit-econ & pricing next steps / pilot proposal

Elena / Jae — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side.

Call recap (30m):
- Goals: productionize LLM-powered insights for transaction monitoring (real-time scoring + batch enrichment).
- Expected user signals: ~5M tokens/week in steady state, short-term pilot traffic ~1–2M tokens/week, peak bursts up to ~20M tokens/week during month-end.
- Key commercial constraints: procurement prefers predictable spend, target internal metric is <$1,000 per 1M tokens for initial phase; product team asking for $/feature estimates and CAC payback assumptions.

Immediate asks for you (so we align proposal):
1) Confirm expected monthly budget range (ballpark is fine).
2) Confirm which features are mandatory for pilot (real-time scoring only vs scoring + enrichment).
3) Any procurement timelines / PO cadence we should plan for?

What I attached: finserve_unit_econ_model.xlsx — a working model that maps tokens -> $/1M, per-feature cost, and basic CAC payback inputs. I filled in a few reasonable assumptions (you can overwrite).

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm items 1–3 above (reply to this thread).
- We produce a short Pricing + Unit-Econ memo and a 6-week pilot pact (pilot credit + capped run-rate).
- Aim to present to procurement the week of 3/22 if timelines align.

Happy to jump on a quick 20m follow-up if helpful.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0189

Attachment: finserve_unit_econ_model.xlsx (spreadsheet, 45KB)
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finserve.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jae Kim <jae.kim@finserve.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: Unit-econ & pricing next steps / pilot proposal

Thanks, Sergio — useful recap. Quick answers and a couple of clarifying items: 

1) Budget range: For initial pilot we can allocate $2,500–$7,500/month depending on ingress. If results look promising we can scale to $25k–$75k/month within 6–9 months. Procurement will need a predictable run-rate for forecasting.
2) Pilot features: must include real-time scoring + the small enrichment payload (adds ~20% token volume on average).
3) Procurement timeline: we have a standing review on 3/25; earlier is better but 3/25 is the conservative target for approvals. PO lead time historically ~3–4 weeks once legal confirms terms.

Specific asks for your proposal: 
- Please map $/1M tokens to the feature-level: e.g., cost per scoring-only feature vs scoring+enrichment. We need to show PM and finance how $/feature maps to their OKRs.
- Include assumptions behind CAC payback (we target <9 months; need to see starter inputs you used).
- We are sensitive to gross margin erosion — finance expects inference cost to be <15% of feature P&L contribution in year 1.

I uploaded a small sample of expected request profiles to the Drive link in case it helps.

Elena
VP Product — Risk Solutions
FinServe Corp

Attachment: prod-usage-sample.csv (3KB)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 17:00:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Unit-econ & pricing next steps / pilot proposal

Monica / Marissa — forwarding FinServe's reply and asks. Key takeaways: pilot budget $2.5k–7.5k/mo, steady state could grow to $25k–75k/mo. They require feature-level $/1M token mapping and CAC payback <9 months; finance wants inference cost <15% of feature P&L in year 1.

Can you help with:
- A compact two-sheet proposal: 1) pricing tiers + recommended pilot credit; 2) unit-econ memo that translates tokens -> $/feature (assume average tokens per scoring call = 120; enrichment adds 24 tokens).
- Recommended $/1M tokens we can offer for pilot vs committed run-rate (goal: protect margin, be competitive vs their $1k/1M target).
- Any strategic discount / credit we can present to shorten CAC payback (e.g., free onboarding, marketing co-sell credit).

I attached a draft proposal (pricing-proposal-draft.pdf) with a starter number: $/1M tokens = $650 for committed 50M/mo equivalent; pilot rate $450/1M with $5k credit. I'm not married to these numbers — want your input.

Also: if legal needs to accelerate, happy to involve AM/Legal early. Procurement wants to see a simple MSA + SOW template.

Thanks — would like to send a clean proposal back to Elena by EOD 3/17.

Sergio
(attachment: pricing-proposal-draft.pdf)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finserve.com>, Jae Kim <jae.kim@finserve.com>, procurement@finserve.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 19:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: Unit-econ & pricing next steps / pilot proposal

Elena / Jae — appreciate the clarity. Attached is a short Pricing + Unit-Econ memo that directly maps your traffic profiles to feature-level costs and to CAC-payback assumptions. Highlights: 

- Pilot plan (6 weeks): pilot credit $5,000 + dedicated onboarding. Pilot rate: $450 per 1M tokens (applies only to pilot usage).
- Committed run-rate offer (if commit >= 50M tokens/month for 6 months): $650 per 1M tokens. This maps to ~58% gross margin at our standard implementation/cost model given the profiling you shared (average request = 144 tokens after enrichment).
- $/feature example (based on your sample):
  - Scoring-only call (avg 120 tokens) -> ~$54 per 1,000 calls (equates to ~$450 / 1M tokens pilot rate).
  - Scoring + enrichment (avg 144 tokens) -> +20% token uplift -> ~$65 per 1,000 calls at pilot rate.
- CAC payback: with our proposed pilot package and a conservative conversion rate (pilot -> paid = 35%), our model shows CAC payback ~7–9 months depending on conversion velocity. I included the base CAC assumptions we used in the attached spreadsheet.

Next steps we propose: 
1) We send a short SOW + MSA (terms we typically use) for your procurement to review — target to have that to you by 3/22.
2) Run the 6-week pilot on pilot terms after procurement OKs the SOW; onboarding to begin within 5 business days of SOW execution.
3) Parallel technical kickoff: schedule 60m integration demo with our engineering CS team — we are available 3/23 or 3/24.

If the pricing above is aligned, I'll prepare a one-page commercial term sheet to route to procurement. If you need tighter unit-econ at the feature level or lower pilot pricing, tell me which levers are most important and we'll adjust (e.g., longer commit, higher volume floors, marketing co-sell).

HubSpot link to deal record: https://hubspot.redwood.company/deal/DS-4589
Drive with models: https://drive.redwood.company/finserve/

Thanks, looking forward to next steps.

Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0189

Attachments: pricing-proposal-draft.pdf (12KB), finserve_unit_econ_model.xlsx (45KB)
summary: Post-call sales thread for FinServe: confirmed pilot budget range, required feature set, requested feature-level $/1M token mapping, and CAC payback assumptions. Proposal: 6-week pilot with $5k credit at $450/1M; committed rate $650/1M at >=50M/mo; next steps SOW/MSA and technical kickoff.
